claim: Preflop charts should be treated as baseline range shapes whose branch changes with position, depth, open size, rake and the players left to act.
interpretation: The trainer should teach a compact decision architecture around the baseline rather than require memorisation of every mixed chart cell.
assumptions: The learner has a reasonable baseline range shape
Exact chart weights are not required for the current decision
exceptions: Exact hand boundaries and frequencies remain visual-dependent
Large rake or unusual sizing can move marginal hands across the boundary
rake_or_structure_notes: Rake, ante/no-ante and straddle structure materially change range shape
notes: No exact chart cells are reproduced.

claim: A poor passive call does not automatically create a profitable bluff 3-bet; the raised branch must be evaluated against the stronger range that continues.
interpretation: Call, 3-bet and fold are separate branches. Initiative is not a sufficient reason to convert a marginal hand into aggression.
assumptions: Villain's continuing range becomes stronger after facing the 3-bet
No special read creates exceptional fold equity
exceptions: A hand can still become a bluff 3-bet when it gains enough from folds and has useful blockers/equity
positions: All positions, especially SB and squeeze branches
rake_or_structure_notes: Rake can reduce the value of marginal passive calls
notes: Mechanism claim only; no fixed combo prescription.

claim: When live opponents enter too widely, a disciplined squeeze exploit increases the use of existing mixed candidates before inventing new bluff combinations.
interpretation: Exploit expansion should preserve coherent range shape: increase justified candidates with fold equity and playability rather than add arbitrary suited hands.
assumptions: Opponent open/call ranges are genuinely wider than baseline
The candidate already exists in a defensible mixed or polar 3-bet region
exceptions: If opponents continue too much, the range should shift more linear rather than add polar bluffs
sizing_scope: Open plus call facing a squeeze
notes: Exact positions, sizes and combo weights remain claim-gated.

claim: Deeper stacks increase the value of suited playability and protected flats, while shorter stacks shift more weight toward direct linear aggression and earlier stack commitment.
interpretation: The trainer should teach the directional depth shift without pretending to know an exact stack threshold or hand matrix from audio alone.
assumptions: Same positions and broadly similar opponent model
No extreme rake or sizing discontinuity
exceptions: Exact stack-off thresholds and hand frequencies remain visual-dependent
Opponent-specific folds can override the baseline direction
rake_or_structure_notes: Straddle changes the working depth unit
conflicts: Exact depth overlays remain open and must not be inferred from this directional claim
